description: Government-backed margin money subsidy of 25%-35% for setting up new micro-enterprises in rural and urban areas. Rural applicants receive higher subsidy rates. Project cost ceiling is ₹50 Lakh for manufacturing and ₹20 Lakh for service/trade sectors.

Collateral-free institutional micro-credit under three tiers — Shishu (up to ₹50K), Kishore (₹50K–₹5L), and Tarun (₹5L–₹10L) — for non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises. Loans are available through banks, MFIs, and NBFCs.

Bank loans between ₹10 Lakh and ₹1 Crore for greenfield enterprises in manufacturing, services, or trading. Targets at least one SC/ST and one woman entrepreneur per bank branch. Covers up to 75% of project cost.

scheme_name: PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME)
description: Credit-linked capital subsidy of 35% (max ₹10 Lakh) for individual micro food processing units. Supports existing and new units in One District One Product (ODOP) categories including bakery, spices, pickles, dairy, and grain milling.

Capital subsidy of 25%-33.33% for setting up small dairy farms (minimum 2 milch animals), calf rearing, milk chilling, and value-added dairy product units. Back-ended subsidy routed through NABARD to commercial and cooperative banks.

scheme_name: Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro & Small Enterprises (CGTMSE)
description: Collateral-free credit facility with up to 85% credit guarantee coverage for loans up to ₹2 Crore. No third-party guarantee or collateral required. Available for both new and existing MSEs through eligible lending institutions.

Medium-to-long term debt financing with 3% annual interest subvention (up to ₹2 Crore) and CGTMSE credit guarantee for post-harvest management infrastructure — cold storage, warehousing, sorting, grading, and packaging facilities.

scheme_name: PM SVANidhi – Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi
description: Affordable collateral-free working capital loan of ₹10K–₹50K with 7% interest subsidy and cashback incentive for digital transactions. Targets street vendors, hawkers, and micro-retailers in urban and semi-urban areas.
